title: A page's own fields — living-docs capability
description: The fields that make a document a page of a documentation space, in its front matter (living-docs DEC-001 point 4): `reader`, who the page is for, and `kind`, which kind of page it is and so which template it follows. A document is a page only if it carries them; a decision record, a rule-set file and what another component claims never is. They are the page's own fields, outside the methodology's container: its friction block sits in the container and is the core's, validated by the backbone (COR-050, COR-053 point 10). Every other front-matter field is the page's business and is not constrained here. Applied by the capability's validator, `pkit living-docs validate` (the `living-docs:spaces` member of `pkit validate`), to every document in a space's places that carries either field — a Markdown page binds by those fields, not by `pkit_schema:` or `binds_to:`, which bind YAML data files (COR-023). This schema fixes the shape of `reader`; the validator also resolves it against the readers point, `pkit::documentation:readers`, and fails a page whose reader the point does not hold.

reader.description: The reader the page is for: the id of an entry of the readers point (DEC-001 point 7) — `user` and `maintainer` by default. One reader; the page says only what that reader needs (RS-LDOC-003).

kind.description: The page's kind, named by the template it follows: pages of a kind follow one format, with a template per kind (RS-LDOC-004). The capability ships the `signpost` template (RS-LDOC-005); a kind is a word, and a kind other than the shipped ones arrives with its template.

word.description: A lowercase letter, then lowercase letters, digits and hyphens.
